A Matter of the Third Lamp

bakerstreetirregular

Summary:

Holmes, the rain, and a lamp that burns the wrong colour.

Work Text:

It was the third lamp from the corner that Holmes would not leave alone.

“Two of them burn yellow,” he said, standing at our window with his pipe gone cold, “and the third burns white. A lamplighter does not carry two kinds of oil, Watson. Somebody else has been at that post.”

I said, with some justice, that a man might simply have cleaned the glass.

“Then he cleaned it at four in the morning, in the rain, and left no mark of his boots on the step.” He set the pipe down. “No. Somebody wished to be seen by one particular window, and only that one. We have only to find out which.”

We found out by supper. It was ours.

Notes:

Thank you for reading all the way to the lamps. This was written for a prompt about small kindnesses; the prompt-giver knows who they are.
